primary_verdict: proved as written for the exact geometric and sufficient-vertex-budget statements in this module
scope: RegularPolygon.lean only. This is not an audit verdict that full P47 has been integrated or verified.

claim_card.objects: Actual finite regular-polygon vertices exp(2*pi*i*j/n), convex hull of their range, arbitrary circle rotation q, nonnegative attenuation alpha, exact real eta and natural-number ceiling.
claim_card.hypotheses: Finite support for the abstract hull lemma; n>=3 for regular-polygon inradius and invariance; alpha>=0 and alpha<=cos(pi/n); eta>0 for the sufficient ceiling count.
conclusions: The closed radius-r ball is contained in the finite convex hull when actual support in every direction is at least norm(v)*r.
The regular polygon is closed and convex, contains the disk of radius cos(pi/n), and lies in the unit disk.
Zero belongs for n>=3 and one belongs for n>0.
Every arbitrary unit rotation followed by attenuation alpha<=cos(pi/n) preserves the actual polygon.

obligation_matrix.obligation: HB separator orientation and Riesz dictionary
obligation_matrix.evidence: Hahn-Banach yields f(p)<u<f(z). Riesz gives f(x)=inner(v,x). Cauchy-Schwarz and norm(z)<=r give f(z)<=norm(v)*r<=f(p), contradiction. No desired disk inclusion is assumed.

obligation_matrix.obligation: All requested regular polygon geometry concerns actual finite vertices/hull
obligation_matrix.evidence: polygon is convexHull of range(vertex n); support comes from the compiled angle/finite modulo-index module, not a supplied inradius.
Every actual vertex has norm1, convexity of the closed unit ball gives hull inclusion; j=0 gives the actual vertex1.
Unit-circle norm multiplicativity gives norm(alpha*q*z)=alpha*norm(z)<=alpha<=cos(pi/n), hence actual inradius membership.
The ceiling/max bound gives pi/n<=sqrt(2*eta); squaring nonnegative values and 1-x^2/2<=cos(x) give the target. No numerical approximation is used.

n=0 is admitted only for unconditional empty-hull closedness/outer-ball inclusion. n>=3 prevents zero denominator and supplies nonnegative cos radius. v=0 requires no cancellation, and the strict separation contradiction excludes zero separators automatically. eta>1 still satisfies the stronger geometric budget lemma; alpha=1-eta nonnegativity is a separate application condition.

obligation_matrix.evidence: These are not claims in RegularPolygon.lean and require the approximation/instrument modules and their explicit domain/positivity/policy contracts.
